writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Faced with growing globalization,students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture helps cultivate cultural confidence." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
writing.sample: Faced with growing globalization,students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture helps cultivate cultural confidence. In an age when Western brands, movies and festivals flood daily life, many young people begin to look back at their own roots. They find that cultural confidence cannot be borrowed from outside; it must grow from real knowledge of what their ancestors created.The reason is not hard to understand. Globalization exposes us to different values, yet it also makes us question who we are. Only by learning the ideas behind Confucianism, the beauty of calligraphy, or the spirit of traditional festivals can we answer that question with pride. Take the Spring Festival as an example: those who understand its meaning of reunion and renewal celebrate it not out of habit, but out of identity.Therefore, college students should actively read classics, visit museums and practice folk arts. The deeper we understand traditional Chinese culture, the more confident we become in facing the world.

Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

transcript.en: M: Welcome to "Business Matters". Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work. Hi, Lucy. Many of us never seem to get promoted. Why is that? And what can we do about it?
transcript.zh: M: 欢迎收听《商业纵横》。今天我们邀请了职业发展顾问露西·威廉姆斯，来谈谈如何在职场上取得成功。你好，露西。我们很多人似乎一直得不到晋升，这是为什么？我们又能做些什么呢？

transcript.en: W: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses. It's important to expand your network and include your co-workers.
transcript.zh: W: 人们常犯的一个错误，是把沟通对象局限在自己的上司。拓展人际网络很重要，也要把同事纳入其中。

transcript.en: M: But some of our co-workers are less senior to us. Is it really necessary to connect with them?
transcript.zh: M: 但我们有些同事的职位比我们低。真的有必要和他们建立联系吗？

transcript.en: W: It's important not to underestimate your colleagues. Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.
transcript.zh: W: 重要的是不要低估你的同事。有时候，职位名称并不能清楚地体现他们可能拥有的影响力。

transcript.en: M: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn't always true, is it?
transcript.zh: M: 现在我们很多人都认为努力工作会给别人留下好印象，但事实并不总是如此，对吧？

transcript.en: W: That's right. We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late, just to show that you are committed.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。我们应该避免为了表现出自己的投入，就试图承担过多的工作，还总是加班到很晚。

transcript.en: M: I see. So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don't maintain them.
transcript.zh: M: 我明白了。所以，一开始就把别人对我们的期待设得太高，如果后来无法保持，就可能让我们看起来很糟糕。

transcript.en: W: Yeah, it's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time. And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.
transcript.zh: W: 是的，最好确保自己投入的是高质量的时间，而不只是大量的时间。而且，我们取得的成果很容易证明这些努力。

transcript.en: M: What about helping others at work? Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?
transcript.zh: M: 那么，在工作中帮助别人呢？你是否应该尽力超越自己的日常职责，主动提出帮助别人完成项目？

transcript.en: W: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended. If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.
transcript.zh: W: 向那些需要帮助的人提供援助，但前提是不能让自己的工作无人处理。如果有人能从你的帮助或建议中获益，就帮他们一把，以赢得他们的尊重和信任。

transcript.en: M: But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all, otherwise you'll appear arrogant.
transcript.zh: M: 不过，显而易见，你不应该表现得像个无所不知的人，否则会显得傲慢。

transcript.en: W: Absolutely. Be humble, and you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.
transcript.zh: W: 当然。保持谦逊，之后你会有很多时间展现自己的才华。

transcript.en: W: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities. From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion. That would mean altogether, we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.
transcript.zh: W: 我觉得我们首先需要决定如何分配演示的任务。据我所记得，这次演示由五个部分组成，不包括开头和结尾。也就是说，我们总共需要在我们两个人之间分配七个部分。

transcript.en: M: So, we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results and the discussion portions. As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation. How would you suggest we dole out the rest?
transcript.zh: M: 所以，我们有摘要、背景研究、项目设计、结果和讨论这几个部分。由于摘要部分只适用于文章，我们不必把它包括在演示中。你建议我们如何分配剩下的部分？

transcript.en: W: How do you feel about handling the background bit? In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.
transcript.zh: W: 你觉得由你来负责背景研究部分怎么样？这样一来，我们就都可以讲述自己投入最多时间的项目部分了。

transcript.en: M: Hold on a minute. You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation? The background research which was so meticulous took more than a month.
transcript.zh: M: 等一下。你是想让我这个承担了大部分任务的人，再负责演示的大部分内容？那份一丝不苟的背景研究花了一个多月的时间。

transcript.en: W: OK. OK. I get it. Quit your moaning. I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it. What do you think would be a fair arrangement?
transcript.zh: W: 好了，好了。我明白了。别再抱怨了。我认可你在研究中所表现出的严谨工作态度，但不欣赏每次我提到这件事时你表现出的讽刺。你觉得怎样分配才公平？

transcript.en: M: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts: before-1980 and afterward. I would take the before-portion and you would be assigned the after-1980, leaving the project and results. I volunteer to describe the project. But as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?
transcript.zh: M: 我觉得最好的安排是把研究分成两部分：1980年以前和之后。我负责1980年以前的部分，你负责1980年以后的部分，项目设计和结果部分则另行分配。我自愿介绍项目设计。不过，我在结果部分的统计数据方面有些吃力，你来负责那一部分怎么样？

transcript.en: W: That's agreeable to me. I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.
transcript.zh: W: 我觉得这样可以。我提议我们分段负责讨论部分，之后的问答环节也由我们共同完成，这样就只剩下开头和结尾了。

transcript.en: M: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction. This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.
transcript.zh: M: 我来负责结尾，你来负责开头。这样我们就可以交替进行演示，避免让听众觉得单调。

transcript.en: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse. According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
transcript.zh: 化妆不仅能改变你的外表，还能改变他人对你的看法，结果可能更好，也可能更糟。根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的一项新研究，虽然男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性会将化妆与有声望、积极的品质联系起来，而女性则认为化妆的其他女性更具支配性，并可能构成威胁。

transcript.en: The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.
transcript.zh: 研究表明，男性和女性都认为化妆后的面孔更具吸引力，但只有女性认为化妆后的面孔更具支配性，只有男性认为化妆后的面孔具有更高的声望。

transcript.en: A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female-on-female jealousy seemed to be the main cause of the differences in perception. Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-makeup wearing counterparts.
transcript.zh: 一项后续研究探究了这些认知差异背后的根本原因，发现女性之间的嫉妒似乎是造成这种认知差异的主要原因。对化妆女性进行评价的女性表示，她们会更嫉妒这些女性，并认为相比不化妆的女性，她们对男性更具吸引力。

transcript.en: Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face. It can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others' perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others' trust and admiration. At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate's decision about wearing makeup. Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant and prestigious can affect the interviewers' actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.
transcript.zh: 化妆品的作用不只是让你拥有一张漂亮的脸。对于女性而言，了解化妆如何改变他人对自己的看法，尤其是在试图赢得他人的信任和钦佩时，可能非常有用。在求职面试中，了解招聘委员会由男性还是女性组成，可能会影响女性求职者是否化妆的决定。面试官是否会认为她具有吸引力、支配性和声望，可能会影响面试官的行为，甚至可能影响面试本身的结果。

transcript.en: You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever. But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower? To answer this question, we first have to ask: "What is willpower?" Most people, sadly, think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations. In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun. No wonder people hope to make changes without it.
transcript.zh: 你可能见过一些广告大肆宣扬无需任何意志力就能改变习惯的方法。但你真的能够在没有意志力的情况下改掉坏习惯或养成好习惯吗？要回答这个问题，我们首先必须问：“什么是意志力？”遗憾的是，大多数人只把它看作咬紧牙关、抵制诱人诱惑的能力。在这种看法中，意志力意味着自我克制和毫无乐趣。难怪人们希望不借助意志力就能做出改变。

transcript.en: I define willpower as "using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions." Let's say your motivators are "prevent diabetes" and "reach a healthy weight". So if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator—avoid diabetes through weight loss—and you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.
transcript.zh: 我把意志力定义为“仅凭想到自己的动机来控制行为”。假设你的动机是“预防糖尿病”和“达到健康体重”。那么，当你在自助餐厅面对不限量供应的食物时，你会想到自己的动机——通过减重来避免糖尿病——于是少量取食，并避开甜点区。

transcript.en: So, amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought—a bright idea—some way to improve your life or contribute to others. This bright idea is your motivator.
transcript.zh: 所以，令人惊讶的是，意志力始于一个想法——一个改善生活或为他人做出贡献的好主意。这个好主意就是你的动机。

transcript.en: Doctor Walter Mischel, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term "a burning goal". Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.
transcript.zh: 意志力技能专家沃尔特·米歇尔博士使用了“一个燃烧的目标”这一生动的说法。无论你把它称为动机、燃烧的目标，还是好主意，这个想法都是意志力背后的力量。

transcript.en: What sort of bright ideas—motivators—make for effective willpower? In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts. The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, a personal mission and being a role model for your child. All these can certainly drive a positive change.
transcript.zh: 什么样的好主意——也就是动机——能够产生有效的意志力？事实上，任何一个你高度重视的目标都算在内。这个清单可能包括良好的健康状况、自尊、为家人创造更美好的未来、个人使命，以及成为孩子的榜样。所有这些都确实能够推动积极的改变。

transcript.en: For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying. In part, that's because the federal government's advice on the matter, first issued in 2004, has long been criticized as vague. That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat, and which species pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination. But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breastfeeding women away from eating seafood altogether.
transcript.zh: 对许多孕妇来说，了解哪些海产品安全且有益健康，以及哪些海产品因担心汞而应当避免，会带来许多忧虑。部分原因在于，联邦政府首次于2004年发布的相关建议长期以来一直被批评含糊不清。该指导意见包括关于应食用多少海产品，以及孕妇和哺乳期女性因担心汞污染而应避免哪些种类的建议。但批评者表示，政府的这份指导意见弊大于利，使许多孕妇和哺乳期女性彻底不敢食用海产品。

transcript.en: The problem is real. According to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA for short, the agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1,000 pregnant women in the US and found that 21 per cent of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month. And those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines. Some 50 per cent ate less than two ounces a week and 75 per cent ate less than four ounces.
transcript.zh: 这个问题确实存在。据美国食品药品监督管理局（简称FDA）一位发言人介绍，该机构分析了美国一千多名孕妇的鱼类食用数据，发现其中21%在前一个月完全没有吃鱼。而那些吃鱼的人，摄入量也远低于膳食指南的建议。约50%的人每周摄入量少于两盎司，75%的人少于四盎司。

transcript.en: This week the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than sixty species in a chart that ranks fish as A Best Choice, Good Choice and Choices to Avoid. The goal is to make it easier for mothers-to-be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets. The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat, and it comes with an easy-to-understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be—four ounces for an adult and two ounces for children aged four to seven.
transcript.zh: 本周，FDA更新了相关建议，在一张图表中列出六十多种鱼类，并将其分为“最佳选择”“不错的选择”和“应避免的选择”。此举旨在让准妈妈更容易对自己饮食中所摄入的海产品种类感到放心。新建议推荐消费者食用多种鱼类，并配有一幅易于理解的图示，说明适当的食用分量应为多少：成年人四盎司，四至七岁的儿童两盎司。

transcript.en: And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid. But not everyone is thrilled with the new advice. Critics say the new advice doesn't always agree with the agency's own scientific findings. While mercury is of great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it's not the only factor contributing to anxiety.
transcript.zh: 长期以来，准妈妈一直被告诫要避开鲨鱼以及另外四种来自墨西哥湾的特定鱼类，而现在，又有三种鱼类被列入应避免食用的名单。但并非所有人都对这份新建议感到满意。批评者表示，新建议并不总是与该机构自己的科学研究结果一致。人们谈论孕妇和海产品时，汞确实是非常令人担忧的因素，但它并不是导致焦虑的唯一因素。

transcript.en: The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis. Agency spokesman Cassell says the FDA believes their recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty. But critics disagree. They think the FDA's advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.
transcript.zh: FDA坚持认为，其最终的食用建议是基于全面的科学分析制定的。该机构发言人Cassell表示，FDA相信这些建议将增强信心，而不是增加不确定性。但批评者对此并不认同。他们认为，FDA的建议并没有以其自身那份详细报告中的证据为依据，因此让所有人都感到困惑。

transcript.en: I know you're busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries. So, should you plan one big vacation for the year, or should you take multiple short vacations throughout? Quantity can sometimes beat quality. First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them, and soon. The longer you put off your time off, the worse you're making things for yourself.
transcript.zh: 我知道你忙于工作，但你也需要抽出一些时间休息，让自己的精力得到恢复。那么，你应该为这一年安排一次长假，还是应该在全年安排多次短假？数量有时胜过质量。首先，无论你如何使用假期，都需要真正使用它们，而且要尽快使用。你越是推迟休假，就越是在让自己的处境变得糟糕。

transcript.en: One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease. So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself. Give yourself a break, folks.
transcript.zh: 《心身医学》发表的一项为期9年的研究表明，每年至少不休一次假，可能会增加因心脏病死亡的风险。所以，你不仅是在扼杀自己的快乐，也可能是在置自己于死地。各位，给自己放个假吧。

transcript.en: When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors: how many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play. Because of that, there's no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for. We know that in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between 7 and 11 days long. That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up, and achieve full-on calm.
transcript.zh: 不过，你应该在什么时候休假，取决于几个因素：你有多少天可用假期、哪些活动能给你带来快乐、你是否有家庭，以及其他会产生影响的变量。正因为如此，并不存在适用于所有人的完美公式，但还是有几件事是每个人都可以努力做到的。我们知道，就最大限度地放松而言，你应该争取安排7到11天的假期。这样你就有足够的时间摆脱工作压力，彻底放松下来，达到完全平静的状态。

transcript.en: That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. Eight days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year. But if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced 8-day vacations a year. If you have 14 days of paid leave, that's almost three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds.
transcript.zh: 上述研究还建议你把假期均匀地分散开来，而不是一次性用完所有假期。对于一年只有10天假期的人来说，8天听起来可能很多。但如果把周末安排在假期前后，你一年就可以安排两次间隔均匀的8天假期。如果你有14天带薪休假，那几乎可以安排三次分别为8天的假期，用来把一年分成三个阶段。

transcript.en: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency. Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier. If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.
transcript.zh: 尽管把所有假期都用来享受一次漫长的暑假可能很有吸引力，但你的总体目标应该是在假期长度、愉悦感和休假频率之间取得完美平衡。休假频率很重要，因为在全年安排多次休息意味着你总有值得期待的事情。筹划事情以及随之而来的期待往往会让我们更加快乐。如果你每年只休一次长假，兴奋感会积累得慢得多，而且由于假期看起来遥不可及，实际上可能会让人产生绝望感。

transcript.en: Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or caught in the heat of an argument are being developed in Sweden. Researchers working as part of the European Union's €77 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired. If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents. Doctor Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is. She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.
transcript.zh: 在瑞典，人们正在研发能够在驾驶员疲劳或陷入激烈争论时接替其驾驶的自动驾驶汽车。作为欧盟770亿欧元研究计划一部分开展工作的研究人员，正在开发基于传感器的系统，用于监测驾驶员是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。如果驾驶员的状态不适合上路，汽车会自动接管方向盘，以防止发生事故。负责该项目的瑞典国家道路与运输研究所安娜·阿农博士表示，可以利用多种传感器测量驾驶员的状态，包括心率监测器和眼部传感器，后者可以追踪驾驶员的视线方向。她说，目标是真正确保从驾驶员到车辆的控制权转换以安全的方式完成，这样我们就能考虑到驾驶员的状态，也不会把控制权交给正承受疲劳、压力、焦虑等影响的驾驶员。

transcript.en: According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second. However, the number of road accidents in both has largely levelled out since 2010. Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen. At 6:00 a.m., for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10:00 a.m. While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.
transcript.zh: 根据欧盟委员会的数据，瑞典拥有欧盟最安全的道路，英国紧随其后。不过，自2010年以来，两国的道路事故数量基本趋于平稳。据认为，驾驶员疲劳要对欧盟范围内多达五分之一的道路事故负责，尽管一天中某些时段发生的事故更多。例如，据称驾驶员在早上6点发生事故的可能性是在上午10点时的20倍。尽管大多数专家都认为，从长远来看，无人驾驶技术应有助于降低事故数量，但一些人质疑其是否安全。

transcript.en: The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between Level 3 on the autonomy scale, in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and Level 4, in which driving is automated.
transcript.zh: 研究人员表示，他们正在开发的技术旨在弥合自动驾驶等级体系中第3级与第4级之间的差距：在第3级，驾驶员必须随时准备接管汽车；而在第4级，驾驶过程实现自动化。

transcript.en: Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK's connected and autonomous vehicle programme Meridian, said: "there is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a Level 3 car completely safe." Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment. With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
transcript.zh: 英国互联与自动驾驶汽车项目Meridian的首席执行官丹尼尔·鲁伊斯说：“关于如何让第3级汽车完全安全，目前正在展开激烈的讨论。”尽管技术取得了进步，但要改变公众的看法，我们仍有一段路要走。随着近期引人关注的事故增多，如今驾驶员认为自动驾驶汽车不如过去安全。

passage.t: Imagine you and a stranger are sitting on a couch. How close would you sit to them? It turns out that how much of a
zone you prefer may reveal a lot about your personality. In one study, researchers sought to
how our personality may be linked to our preferred amount of personal space. The researchers found that people who scored higher in the
of agreeableness tended to sit closer to others, as did people who were more open and outgoing. Other individual differences, such as gender and age, can also affect how much personal space we

. Women tend to prefer more physical distance from strangers or acquaintances and older adults also generally tend to prefer to keep more distance between themselves and others. Beyond reflecting our personality and

, the amount of personal space we prefer is also linked to our cultural backgrounds. In a study involving participants from 42 countries, researchers found that around the world people's desired amount of personal space varied
. For example, in Romania, the average amount of personal space people said they would prefer from a stranger was more than 4 feet, whereas in Argentina it was roughly half that. What might
this variation? The researchers looked at a number of
factors, but the only one that was significantly

with preferred interpersonal distance was average temperature. The warmer the place, it seems, the "warmer" the people and the less space they needed between them and others. Personal space may also reflect interpersonal attraction. Researchers have found that our chosen physical
also appears to reflect how much we like others. The more people would like to be friends with the other person, the closer they sat to them.

matching.title: It's never too early to teach children about money

paragraphs.t: The cost of a mortgage or rents, meeting monthly utility bills, paying for a new car—all headaches most people get to worry about from their 20s. But while some may struggle to pay their bills after a few too many nights out at the start of the month, others will have a tightly followed plan for their repayments. So what is the difference between the shrewd saver and the more reckless spender?

Experts believe it is all about the age you learn how to spend responsibly. Adult money habits are typically set by the age of seven, according to a large-scale study by the government's Money Advice Service and behaviour experts at Cambridge University. By then, most children have grasped how to recognise the value of money and are capable of complex functions such as planning ahead, delaying a decision until later and understanding that some choices are irreversible.

Tomorrow marks the start of Global Money Week, a worldwide initiative to help children make smart financial decisions and learn that "money matters matter". But for many young people in the UK, it's a matter of too little, too late. "The habits of mind which influence the ways children approach complex problems and decisions, including financial ones, are largely determined in the first few years of life," says Dr David Whitebread, the co-author of the study. And this core behaviour is very likely to influence their financial decisions when they are adults, he says.

The study also urges parents not to underestimate their own good and bad money habits. "Since young children have few monetary resources they control independently, it is the basic approaches and skills which are modelled, discussed and demonstrated by parents that are likely to be influential levers, breeding efficient habits and practices," it says.

Parents who choose to help their children learn how to plan ahead, reflect on the past and self-regulate can make a huge difference in promoting good financial behaviour in the future, explains Whitebread. According to a survey by M&G Investments, the vast majority (83%) of parents recognise the value of teaching their children about money. However, this concern does not always carry through to practice—one in six do not feel confident enough to do it. More than one in every four parents think children should take responsibility for understanding money themselves.

"There's joy in the fact that young children are spontaneous and live life in the moment, unrestrained by adult problems. But teaching children about money when they are young is a good way for parents to help them learn to delay satisfaction, so that the child thinks: 'I'd like to do this but I'm not going to'. Hard evidence suggests, if you want your child to do well in life, the earlier you can start trying to teach them inhibition and self-discipline, the better," says Whitebread, pointing to research that has shown people in prison frequently have poor impulse control, a personality trait that can affect relationships and long-term health.
But how should a parent try to teach their child to spend responsibly? One simple way is to give them pocket money and then help them to analyse and learn from any foolish spending decisions.

Another is through board games which can help teach financial responsibility. Pop to the Shops, a shopping board game for five-to-nine-year-olds, has been one of Orchard Toys' top 10 bestselling board games every year for the past 15 years. To win, players must use fake coins to purchase everyday grocery items from various shops around the board, and give the other players who visit their shop the correct change. If they don't have enough money, they must purchase a cheaper item. "It acts as a conversation starter about money —parents can fill in the gaps," says Orchard Toys product manager Rachael Sutcliffe.

There are also some pocket-money-tracking and payment apps, such as RoosterMoney and goHenry, which are designed to be used by under-sevens, and which boast that they can help children develop good money habits. This is dependent on the children receiving enough pocket money to need an app to track their spending, which research suggests is not always the case.

Surprisingly, given the research about habit-forming in young children, there are very few gaming apps that can help under-sevens—Pigby's Fair, developed by NatWest, being a notable exception. In this, children who solve basic puzzles will earn virtual money selling what they have made at different stalls in a fair, then spend or save it. But the need to shift virtual money around, and take into account interest payments and pocket money bonuses, makes it a complex financial education tool.

There are plenty of online games which focus on coin recognition and counting with money, such as the Igloo Shopping game or Top Marks' Coins Game. So what if children find such games boring? An exciting (and free) real-world option for parents to use is a visit to Metro Bank. Although, like most banks, it does not allow children to open an account until they turn 11, it specifically tries to offer young children a chance to learn about money inside its branches by inviting kids to use the "magic money machines" to count their coins. Children who accurately guess how much was in their piggy bank(猪形储钱罐) get a prize, and free candies are handed out when the coins are exchanged for banknotes. The bank does not take a commission from the transaction.

At six years old, my daughter Flora is getting to grips with her finances early. She tested out a number of games aimed at teaching children her age the value of money. She enjoyed them all, but best, in her view, is Money Match Cafe, a board game where she must work out the value of different denominations(面额) of coin in her imaginary restaurant, her "customers" being her stuffed toys. "It was really fun because you get to serve food to your own toys on a little tray with a napkin on it, and then you can hug them," she says.

"If you're six and you play this game, you'll learn that you might not have the right amount of money for what you want to buy. You just have to cross your fingers and hope. It's a good challenge, and I enjoyed adding the coins up to see how much they made. But I don't like the name. Money Match Cafe is not a good name for a cafe. I would have liked it more if it had been Flora's Cafe or Fantastically Baked Lunches."

Seven out of ten teachers think children are now faced with financial decisions earlier. On Wednesday, Lifesavers—a new project which promotes financial education in primary schools—is hosting a conference to encourage teachers to join its programme and get free classroom resources and training. Almost two-thirds of millennials(千禧一代) wish they had received more money advice at a younger age, according to a Santander survey.

Only a third of parents involve their children in discussions about their household finances, even though less than half of young people aged seven to seventeen receive financial education at school, another survey shows.

Most adults believe their parents have had the biggest influence on their money behaviour. So when should they start trying to instil(灌输) good habits? As early as possible before the age of seven, research suggests.

questions.s: Most parents realise the importance of teaching their children how to handle money, but many of them actually don't do much in this respect.
People differ substantially in their way of managing finance.
Parents can easily teach children how to spend responsibly by helping them draw lessons from bad decisions on spending.
Many young British people badly lack money management skills and they don't learn them early enough.
The majority of adults believe that their spending habits have been influenced the most by their parents.
There are apps designed specifically for children under 7 to help them track pocket money spending.
According to experts, the age a person learns to manage finance responsibly determines the way they handle money thereafter.
Most teachers are of the opinion that children today need to make financial decisions at a younger age.
Parents serve as effective role models in shaping children's money management habits.
According to one study, about 30% of parents allow their children to participate in discussions on their family finances.

careful.passage: Three artists have brought a lawsuit against Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney, alleging that the text- to-image AI tools have infringed the rights of thousands of artists. The lawsuit claims that the Stable Diffusion tool used by Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney was trained on billions of copyrighted images downloaded from the internet and used by the companies "without compensation or consent from the artists." The artists are represented by The Joseph Saveri Law Firm and Matthew Butterick. "If Stable Diffusion and similar products are allowed to continue to operate as they do now, the foreseeable result is they will replace the very artists whose stolen works power these AI products with whom they are competing," the law firm wrote in a press release. "AI image products are not just an infringement of artists' rights; they will eliminate 'artist' as a viable career path. In addition to obtaining compensation for the wrongful conduct, this lawsuit seeks to prevent that outcome and ensure these products follow the same rules as any other new technology that involves the use of massive amounts of intellectual property. If streaming music can be accomplished within the law, so can AI products." Since text-to-image generators have increased in popularity in the past year, many artists have been vocalizing their opposition to AI art after seeing their own distorted signatures appear in AI art and finding out that their work was used to train the tools without their permission. Not only are many artists furious at the possible copyright violations of AI art, but they have also been frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes they are required to go through. As a result, many artists have been trying to ban AI art from art-sharing platforms. As AI innovation continues at a rapid speed, it seems that artists and lawmakers are trying to put a brake on further developments before it's too late. Many tech enthusiasts are still rallying around the promise of AI tools to create detailed images cheaply and quickly—anonymous tech supporters have already published a response to Butterick and Joseph Saveri's lawsuit on a website, using the "fair use" clause as the basis for why copyrighted images could be used by the tool. Fair use, a legal doctrine that allows for a limited usage of copyrighted materials without permission by the original creators for purposes such as teaching and news sharing, is what a lot of generative model creators claim that their training data is covered by. However, since fair use applies differently to each case, it's hard to make a blanket statement about all works in a dataset as being applicable.

questions.s: Why have three artists brought a lawsuit against Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney?

o.t: They claim that the use of the Stable Diffusion tool is a violation of law.
They claim these companies infringed their intellectual property rights.
They want to stop the use of all AI tools in the creation of art works.
They want to prevent artists from being compelled to rely on AI tools.

careful.passage: On a warm October morning, Daniel Agok woke up to another disappointing day at his school in Wanyjok, South Sudan. The classes he had planned teaching computer skills to aspiring young professionals were canceled, due to an unreliable diesel generator and the absence of a municipal power grid in his area. Now, he would be losing frustrated customers as well as income. Agok is just one of the hundreds of millions of people in sub- Saharan Africa, many of whom are business owners, who still do not have dependable electricity. This inequitable access to energy continues to put their livelihood and future at risk. The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students. We must instead unleash their abilities and let Africa reach its true economic potential. That means wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy. Historically, national governments on the continent have led electrification efforts, but fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity. This has led to expensive and harmful temporary "solutions". In Nigeria alone experts estimate people spend $13 billion every year on fuel for toxic, polluting generators. That number will only grow as the continent's population hits 2.5 billion people by 2050. Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions with reliable and affordable alternatives. The rapidly growing private power sector in Africa holds the key to achieving the speed and scale necessary to close the continent's energy access gap. Private companies today are building world-class infrastructure and driving forward economic growth with sustainable business models. In fact, many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale. In South Africa, President Cyril Ramaphosa has streamlined licensing requirements and enlisted the private sector to play a key role. South Africa is just one example. Across the continent, the private sector has delivered power faster and more reliably, and governments are increasingly turning to private partners. With the right funding and structure in place, the private sector will come together to provide this essential service. After all, electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity. Today, Daniel Agok is steadily growing his business in South Sudan. His town of Wanyjok was electrified by a private company, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to his business and his neighbors. Agok now operates his growing computer skills training business smoothly. His classes are no longer affected by the smell and the constant noise of the diesel generator, and he saves money with more affordable power. His students are developing hardware and software skills.

questions.s: What do we learn about the current electric supply system in Africa?

o.t: It curbs the economic development of the continent.
It mainly depends on the polluting diesel generators.
It is the primary cause of inequitable distribution of wealth.
It deprives many Africans of the opportunity to use computers.

questions.s: What do we learn from the passage about Africa's past electrification efforts?

o.t: They have failed to meet most Africans' need of a reliable power supply.
They have failed to build a national grid to provide electric power.
They have unleashed the true economic potential of the continent.
They have aimed at wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.

questions.s: What is essential to tackling the power supply shortage in Africa?

o.t: Replacing temporary solutions with long-term strategies.

Putting in place a large-scale modern power grid speedily.

questions.s: What are many governments in Africa doing to solve the electricity supply problem?

o.t: Focusing on building world-class infrastructures.
Relying on the private sector for scale economy.
Launching sustainable business models.
Cooperating with private companies.

questions.s: Why will private companies be motivated to join the effort of electrifying sub-Saharan Africa?

o.t: There is big money to be made.
They have enough funding in place.
South Africa has set a successful example.
Governments are turning to them for help.

translation.source: 近年来，中国无人机(drone) 产业蓬勃发展，出口量跃升为全球第一。中国的无人机以出色的稳 定性、高 清 (high-definition)拍摄能力和便捷的操作，受到全球消费者的喜爱，在民用领域得到广泛应用。无人机已被 国家纳入战略性新兴产业，逐步成为能满足多种场景需求的智能助手。在农村，无人机可精准识别农作物病虫 害，高效喷洒农药。在城市，无人机可快速运送生鲜食品。在不久的将来， 无人机能够在更多领域实现其独 特价值，为经济社会发展注入新动能。
translation.reference: In recent years, China's drone industry has been booming, with its export volume ranking first in the world. Chinese drones are popular with consumers around the world for their excellent stability, high-definition shooting capability and convenient operation, and have been widely used in civilian fields. Drones have been included by the state in strategic emerging industries, and are gradually becoming intelligent assistants that can meet the needs of various scenarios. In rural areas, drones can accurately identify crop diseases and pests, and efficiently spray pesticides. In cities, drones can quickly deliver fresh food. In the near future, drones will be able to realize their unique value in more fields, injecting new momentum into economic and social development.
